text: Code refactoring is the process of improving the structure of existing code without changing what it does. The main goal is to make the code easier to read and understand, which helps developers find and fix problems faster. When you refactor, you reorganize the code, remove duplication, and simplify complex parts. This does not add new features or change how the program behaves for users. Refactoring is important because it reduces technical debt, which is the extra work that builds up when code is messy or poorly written. By cleaning up the code regularly, teams can save time and money in the future.
